rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Poor-quality, damaged or improperly used lithium-ion batteries in e-bikes and e-scooters can cause serious fires.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Lithium-ion battery fires can start without warning, spread rapidly and be difficult to extinguish.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: People should leave the area and call 999 rather than attempt to extinguish an e-bike or e-scooter lithium-battery fire themselves.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Fire risk increases with counterfeit, damaged, poorly manufactured or non-compliant products.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Using an incompatible charger or incompatible replacement parts can increase battery fire risk.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Charging should take place away from escape routes, while the user is awake and present, with the charger unplugged when complete.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Conversion, repair and replacement work should use competent professionals and manufacturer-recommended components.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: E-bike batteries placed on the market must include effective safety protections capable of mitigating thermal runaway during normal use and foreseeable misuse.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: Battery fire risk depends on cell design, manufacturing quality, compatibility, damage, charging behaviour, storage, modification and escape-route conditions.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike and e-scooter battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS e-bike evidence is product-, battery-, charger-, premises-, use- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Button and coin batteries can cause severe injury if swallowed, inserted or ingested, particularly by children and pets.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Coin batteries pose particular risk because their larger size can increase the chance of lodging in the throat.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: A lodged battery can react with saliva and generate caustic soda, causing burns, internal bleeding and potentially death.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Producers should first consider whether a product can avoid using button or coin batteries.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Where batteries are necessary, producers should consider safer alternatives to button or coin cells.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Battery compartments should be securely fastened and resistant to inadvertent opening by children.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Products, packaging and instructions should carry prominent and clear battery hazard warnings.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS encourages producers to follow PAS 7055:2025 and applicable product-specific safety standards.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: Button-battery risk depends on cell size and chemistry, product enclosure, accessibility, warnings, user age, ingestion timing and clinical response.

rows.source: OPSS button and coin battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS button-battery evidence is product-, battery-, user-, exposure- and response-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
